question: Why a new file, directory or transacted storage costs a Windows program 10-76 ms on the console (ole32 storage32 past its budget)

windows_program_per_call_us.tool: tests/lock-probe.c split, in the persistent session (build B2)

native_per_call_us.tool: tools/console-iobench.py --only names (a payload, no title running)

locks: byte-range locks taken, refused, freed with their handle and shared as on the PC (both builds)
verdict: platform limit: the console file system itself takes ~20 ms to create a file and ~23 ms to make a directory; Wine adds no cost to it (its create is cheaper than a native O_EXCL create). ole32 transacted storage makes a scratch file per open, so storage32 needs a longer budget, not a fix.
